newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen leaps to renew contract high.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen leaps to renew contract high.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract ended with substantial gains on Thursday, boosted by concern over the financial health of construction firms and weak industrial output data released late on Wednesday, traders said.
The market turned its focus again to bad loan problems after general contractor Tada Corp said it had applied for court protection under Japanese bankruptcy laws.
The March jumped to its contract high of 99.22 in the morning session amid decisively bullish sentiment.
"The March was bought about two or three ticks during Wednesday's night session," a foreign brokerage trader said.

"Since news about Tokai Kogyo broke out, foreign investors have become very knowledgeable about the plight of general contractors... There is no doubt that the news (about Tada Corp) led to some buying," the trader said. Tokai Kogyo applied for court protection from creditors earlier this month.
But the March surrendered some gains on a rumour a powerful bureaucrat would imply a rate hike possibility, traders said.
The senior trader said that any recovery in production would only be modest because of a gradual rise in corporate inventories.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, some city banks were detected buying four-year fixed interest rates, a city bank trader said.
The four-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.54/58 percent as of 0700 GMT, down from 1.56/60 percent on Wednesday.
The key overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.50 percent, up from the weighted average of 0.49 percent.
